posts.title: Welcome to DevCentr News
posts.description: News and updates across Dev-Centr and related projects — initiatives, shipping notes, and ecosystem changes. (Also indexed as our engineering blog.)
posts.html:
We are starting a public News feed on devcentr.org/news (legacy path: /blog).

What belongs here

  • Initiatives and direction changes across the Dev-Centr org

  • Notable shipping moments on the landing site, docs, and related tools

  • Cross-project news that affects how we build (tooling, formats, sister orgs)

  • Highlights mirrored from Antora changelogs (docs remain the system of record)

This is not a replacement for Antora changelogs or issue trackers. Those stay the system of record for specs and day-to-day work. News is the narrative layer—what we chose, why it matters, and where to dig deeper.

Feeds

  • RSS

  • Atom

Where else to look

  • docs.devcentr.org — knowledge base and specs

  • github.com/dev-centr — source and issues

  • devcentr.app — the flagship app

Expect irregular posts when there is something worth saying—not a content mill.

posts.title: Brand mark and motion format tradeoffs
posts.description: Shipping the DevCentr orbital mark, why we will not hard-advocate Rive, and Popkorn as a potential text-first future. Engineering blog / news update.
posts.html:
We shipped a new org brand mark—an orbital hub meant to read as a center of gravity—and put static + motion assets in the org profile harbor and on the marketing site.

What shipped

  • Transparent and on-dark SVG/PNG sets (including 256px rasters for the GitHub avatar)

  • logo-motion.svg — self-contained CSS motion, no JS player

  • Site chrome uses the same geometry via inline SVG + CSS (LogoMark / HeroOrbit)

Canonical harbor: .github / .github-private profile/ (mirrored under devcentr.org/public/brand/).

Why not “just use Rive”?

Rive is strong for interactive UI motion (state machines, theme inputs). Its runtimes are MIT. The editor is proprietary, and .riv is binary—weak for git diffs and agentic authoring.

So Dev-Centr does not hard-advocate Rive as an open de facto standard. SVG keeps that role for portable marks.

The lanes we document

Lane Prefer when

Animated SVG (+ CSS)

Portable brand loops, docs, READMEs, agent-editable source

Lottie

Complex baked timelines from an AE-shaped pipeline

Rive

Interactive / theme-driven app chrome when a player is already justified

Full write-up: docs.devcentr.org → General Knowledge → Brand and UI Motion Formats (and Recommended Tools).

Potential future: Popkorn

We want a text-first interactive motion format that agents can edit. Popkorn is an early CSS-shaped candidate—not a Dev-Centr default yet.

Outreach / co-op interest on rich interactivity: ayarse/popkorn#7.
